due_when.clears_when: EITHER pr-opener.yml is changed to skip the results write-back when a PR already exists for the head branch (avoiding the extra bot commit entirely), OR this action_required behavior is confirmed as a one-time, harmless GitHub Actions approval gate that self-clears (re-test without a manual rerun and observe).

origin.rerun: Push a branch whose PR is opened by claude-pr-automerge.yml's auto-open path, then also drop a request file for the SAME branch at automation/pr-requests/<slug>.json so pr-opener.yml writes a "results" commit onto the already-open PR; check the new head sha's required-check conclusions via actions_list list_workflow_runs.

what: pr-opener.yml, when it detects a PR already exists for the pushed head (opened separately by claude-pr-automerge.yml, e.g. because the branch is claude/**-prefixed) and writes its results file back onto that SAME branch as a new github-actions[bot]-authored commit: the resulting PR-synchronize checks (pytest-run, pytest-collect, guards, repo-inventory) landed conclusion=action_required instead of running, on PR #13571 (RQ-OPS-2). MEASURED: the checks for the PREVIOUS head sha (pushed under this session's own git identity) ran normally (in_progress/success); only the head sha whose commit was authored by github-actions[bot] via pr-opener's write-back landed action_required. Re-running each stuck run via actions_run_trigger rerun_workflow_run, triggered by an authorized human/session, cleared it and the checks proceeded normally -- so this is a one-time approval gate, not a hard block, but it is silent (no error, just checks that never start) and would strand any PR nobody manually re-triggers.
